newsitem.title: TURKEY: EQUITY, SHARE-DEALING LIMITS PUT ON TURK BROKERS.
newsitem.headline: EQUITY, SHARE-DEALING LIMITS PUT ON TURK BROKERS.

text.p: The Turkish Capital Markets Board (SPK) said on Wednesday it put into effect new rules aimed at achieving a balance between the equities of brokerage houses and the volume of their share transactions.

In a new regulation signed by the SPK chairman Ali Ihsan Karacan, it said the minimum equity of a brokerage house should be 50 billion lira for it to be able to get a licence as an intermediary in share trading.
Brokerages have until June 30, 1997 to fulfill the minimum equity requirement.

An additional equity of 20 billion lira is required for each agency to be set up by a brokerage, 10 billion lira for each branch or representative office, 50 billion lira for each licence to deal in repos and reverse repos on the bond market.

The additional equity requirement is 10 billion lira to obtain a licence to arrange public share offers, another 10 billion lira for a licence in portfolio management and five billion lira for a licence in investment consultancy.
The SPK said brokerages would have to adjust their equities upward every year in line with the official re-evaluation rate to be announced by the Finance Ministry.

Brokerages will also have to deposit as a guarantee four fifths of the minimum equity requirement in the form of state securities at the central depositary Takasbank. One tenth of the amounts exceeding the minimum equity must be blocked at Takasbank in the form of state securities.

The SPK said a single buy or sell order of a brokerage will be limited to 25 percent of its equity and the total volume of share transactions in a day cannot exceed four times its equity. This rule will be retroactively enforced from January 2, 1997.
It said block deals to be made on the wholesale market and special deals based on collateral would be excluded from the share-dealing limits.
Share transactions of brokerages provided with comfort letters after being set up by banks would also be excluded from the above limits.

To boost supervision in the market, the SPK had obliged banks last year to set up or buy separate brokerages with a minimum 125 billion lira capital to handle their share deals from the beginning of 1997.
The total share trading limit will go up to eight times the equity for merged brokerages.
